# Add Telegram Action

1. Decide write vs read first. Writes join TelegramAction and use [`execute()`](mex://function:f58a45f550a495042cf2617134f96b51); reads join TelegramReadAction and use [`execute_read()`](mex://function:a91dba656ea013b32d68a0e7d8d3e08d)/[`execute_read_many()`](mex://function:d8b71cc315512ed3e993315f45cd1413).
2. Define typed action/result contracts in the owning schemas/telegram_actions_*.py module and include them in the correct discriminated union. Re-export public classes from schemas.telegram_actions.
3. Implement Telethon dispatch in the focused core/telegram_client/ module and wire its dispatcher. Both dispatchers match on the concrete action MODEL, not `action_type` (that narrows the type); a body longer than a line goes to a helper, then to a private sibling module once the dispatcher's file nears the size budget — the dispatcher grows by one arm only, and a family one sibling dispatches shares one or-patterned arm. Add that arm deliberately: the write dispatcher ends in one prefix-family arm (`channel_`/`warm_`/`broadcast_` → own dispatcher, via a table) and a profile-media default, so a forgotten arm raises out of the profile-media dispatcher instead of reporting an unsupported action. A new family is a table row, never an arm. Direct and operator-named sends share one helper: decimal recipients become integer peers. A lost acknowledgement after borrowing the client means delivery is unconfirmed; bulk runs report it without retrying. Use raw TL where wrappers hide reads/defaults or run crypto on the loop. Reject unsafe server input before dispatch; offload necessary crypto on a private executor, never the database pool. Own the one read a write needs, because a failure after the client was borrowed reports "may have been applied". A join whose "already inside" is success goes in `execute()`'s join set.
4. Let the public gateway own shared Telegram error/rate-limit classification, including the whole flood family — plain, premium and slow-mode waits plus peer flood, which are not one Telethon subclass. Domain code branches on the typed kind and its seconds; matching the rendered message honours one member and misses the other three. Not every wait is a flood — too-fresh refusals carry seconds while subclassing the generic bad-request error — so a module's own error-code map must leave anything carrying seconds to that gateway ladder instead of flattening a duration into a bare code.
5. Persist durable account/domain state in the service layer. Operator profile/media edits that intentionally make FloodWait sticky must be listed in the profile-edit action set, and only a domain-less call marks it: warming, neurocomment and scheduled posts pass a domain and keep their own retry time.
6. Call the gateway through the domain seam so tests can substitute it.
7. Test success, rate-limit/special classification and generic failure. Patch the symbol on the module that owns it, not a re-exporting package facade.
